scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data” (preprints/The-Gaussian-free-field-limit-of-integer-Lipschitz-heights-with-two-arc-boundary-data-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f0047faf78711628), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let D be a bounded smooth simply connected planar domain with two distinct marked boundary points. Let Dδ be simply connected triangular-lattice polygonal approximations with uniformly converging marked boundary parametrizations and edge-midpoint marks, and let hδ have the uniform odd-height law (1.1). There is a constant σ > 0, depending only on the unit triangular-lattice model, such that hδ =⇒ ḡ + σΦD in D′ (D). For every f ∈ C∞ c (D), Ehδ(f) → ∫ D ḡf. Consequently hδ − Ehδ σ =⇒ ΦD in D′ (D). (1.3) All finite vectors of test-function integrals converge jointly to the corresponding Gaussian vectors, and all their mixed moments converge. The constant is specified by the absolutely convergent finite- volume series in Proposition 6.1; in the spectral convention below, σ = 4π √ c∗.
